critique.evidence: The screen strongly supports an operational defense evaluation: PR-AUC, recall at fixed false-positive budgets, calibration, alert load, latency, confusion counts, ablations, fraud value caught, and good value blocked. The provenance ablation directly suggests intent-integrity relevance. However, the evidence never explicitly connects these measurements to preserved user intent, attack scenarios, Mastercard/payment-network requirements, transaction value, or issuer/merchant outcomes. The unexplained 100% fresh-row recall across every ablation also weakens the claimed defense differentiation.
critique.fix: Add a compact intent-integrity scorecard tied to demonstrated attacks: authorized intent preserved, malicious intent deviations caught, false declines and fraud loss in currency, plus baseline-versus-defense deltas. Explain the invariant 100% fresh-row recall and explicitly map the metrics to Mastercard stakeholders and payment-risk constraints.
